newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Gov Whitman eyes $3.4 bln pension bond sale.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Gov Whitman eyes $3.4 bln pension bond sale.

text.p: New Jersey Governor Christine Whitman is considering a proposal to sell $3.4 billion of pension obligation bonds as part of a plan to shore up the pension system and save money for the state budget, the Governor's spokesman said Monday.
Peter McDonough, Whitman's press secretary, said in a telephone interview that more details about the plan would be made available at a press conference later today by state Treasurer Brian Clymer.
"The Treasurer is looking at a proposal that would refinance at a lower interest rate and for a shorter period of time the outstanding liability of New Jersey's pension system," McDonough said.
"That refinancing would require $3.4 billion in non-general obligation bonds, and would have a net savings to the taxpayer of $1.3 billion," he said.
McDonough said the $1.3 billion savings was calculated on a present value basis.
Whitman came under fire in recent years for lowering the state's annual contribution to the pension system. The move was part of spending cuts tied to her 30 percent income tax reduction package.
